question: My pipe under my slab has burst due to freezing temperatures, how do I repair it?
answer: To repair a burst copper pipe under a concrete slab, first, you'll need to locate the leak. You may need to use a thermal imaging camera to detect the heat loss from the damaged pipe. Once you've found the leak, shut off the water supply and drain the system. You'll then need to remove the concrete slab using a jackhammer or sawzall to expose the pipe. Use a pipe cutter to remove the damaged section of pipe. Clean and deburr the ends of the cut pipe, then apply flux to the ends and solder a new copper coupling in place. Replace the concrete slab and refill the area with concrete.
